title: Towards Efficient Compiler Auto-tuning: Leveraging Synergistic Search Spaces
problem: Determining optimal compiler optimization pass sequences is hard due to exponential search space. Traditional auto-tuning (iterative compilation, ML) incurs high cost and poor generalization. No efficient pruning strategy exists.
motivation: Compiler pass selection directly impacts code quality; efficient auto-tuning enabling fast convergence to near-optimal sequences is critical for practical deployment.
method: The approach tests pairs of compiler optimization passes on benchmark programs and uses clustering (a technique to group similar patterns) to identify which pairs work best when applied in sequence. These successful combinations are collected into a small representative set called a coreset. A machine learning model is then trained on these coresets to predict which combinations will work for new programs without testing each possibility individually. Various search strategies are applied to quickly converge to good solutions.
key_novelty: Identifying synergistic optimization-pass pairs (combinations that work well together) and collecting them into small representative sets (coresets) makes the search space manageable and enables machine learning to predict good strategies for new programs.
contributions: Synergistic pass pair identification via K-means clustering
7.5% average IR instruction reduction vs Oz, 13.9% code size reduction with 5-second search

metrics.other: 7.5% IR reduction, 13.9% code size reduction in 5s

limitations: Evaluation on specific benchmark suites (MiBench, CBench, NPB); generalization to diverse workloads not thoroughly discussed.
primary_theme: efficient compiler auto-tuning via synergistic pass pairs
